questions.question: What is the capital of France?
questions.explanation: Paris has been the capital of France for centuries and sits on the river Seine.

questions.question: Which is the largest ocean on Earth?
questions.explanation: The Pacific covers about a third of the planet's surface.

questions.question: Which river is traditionally considered the longest in Africa?
questions.explanation: The Nile, at roughly 6,650 km, is traditionally cited as the longest river in the world.

questions.question: What is the capital of Australia?
questions.explanation: Canberra was purpose-built as the capital as a compromise between Sydney and Melbourne.

questions.question: What is the capital of Canada?
questions.explanation: Ottawa, in Ontario, has been Canada's capital since 1866.

questions.question: What is the capital of Brazil?
questions.explanation: Brasília was inaugurated as the capital in 1960, replacing Rio de Janeiro.

questions.question: According to United Nations estimates since 2023, which country has the largest population?
questions.explanation: UN estimates indicated that India overtook China in 2023.

questions.question: Mount Everest lies on the border of Nepal and which other country?
questions.explanation: The summit sits on the border between Nepal and the Tibet Autonomous Region of China.

questions.question: Which is the smallest country in the world by area?
questions.explanation: Vatican City covers only about 0.44 square kilometres.

questions.question: Which is the largest hot desert in the world?
questions.explanation: The Sahara covers about 9 million square kilometres. Antarctica is the largest desert overall.

questions.question: Which country has the most time zones, counting its overseas territories?
questions.explanation: France spans about 12 or 13 time zones because of its overseas territories.

questions.question: Which river flows through the centre of Paris?
questions.explanation: The Seine runs through Paris on its way to the English Channel.

questions.question: Which strait separates Spain from Morocco at the entrance to the Mediterranean?
questions.explanation: At its narrowest the Strait of Gibraltar is about 14 km wide.

questions.question: Which is the deepest lake in the world?
questions.explanation: Lake Baikal in Russia reaches about 1,642 metres deep.

questions.question: What is the capital of Turkey?
questions.explanation: Ankara became the capital in 1923. Istanbul is Turkey's largest city.

questions.question: Which continent has the most countries?
questions.explanation: Africa has 54 recognised sovereign states.

questions.question: What is the capital of Kazakhstan?
questions.explanation: The capital was renamed Nur-Sultan in 2019 and returned to the name Astana in 2022.

questions.question: Which two countries share the longest international land border in the world?
questions.explanation: The Canada–US border runs for roughly 8,900 km including the Alaska segment.

questions.question: Which is the largest island in the world?
questions.explanation: Greenland covers about 2.17 million square kilometres. Australia is counted as a continent.

questions.question: In which country is Mount Kilimanjaro?
questions.explanation: Kilimanjaro, Africa's highest peak at 5,895 m, stands in northeastern Tanzania.

questions.question: The Panama Canal connects which two oceans?
questions.explanation: The canal opened in 1914 and shortcuts the long route around South America.

questions.question: Angel Falls, the world's tallest uninterrupted waterfall, is in which country?
questions.explanation: Angel Falls drops 979 metres in Venezuela's Canaima National Park.

questions.question: What is the capital of New Zealand?
questions.explanation: Wellington, at the southern tip of the North Island, is the capital. Auckland is the largest city.

questions.question: Which major city is located on both sides of the Bosphorus, in Europe and in Asia?
questions.explanation: Istanbul straddles the Bosphorus strait, so part of it lies in each continent.

questions.question: Which river is the longest in South America?
questions.explanation: The Amazon is about 6,400 km long and carries more water than any other river.

questions.question: In which country is the historic city of Timbuktu?
questions.explanation: Timbuktu, a medieval centre of trade and learning, lies in Mali.

questions.question: Which is the largest US state by area?
questions.explanation: Alaska covers about 1.7 million square kilometres, more than twice the size of Texas.

questions.question: Which river flows through more countries than any other in the world?
questions.explanation: The Danube flows through ten countries, from Germany to the Black Sea.

questions.question: What is the line of latitude at 0° called?
questions.explanation: The Equator divides the Earth into the Northern and Southern Hemispheres.

questions.question: Which is the smallest continent by land area?
questions.explanation: Australia/Oceania is the smallest, at about 8.5 million square kilometres.
